# Medication mapping draft (generated by `python -m polysafe.medmap`)

**Status: DRAFT for PI review.** Nothing here is accepted until the PI fills `pi_ingredient` / `pi_class` / `pi_reviewed` in `mapping/hicl_draft.csv`.

Method: one key per HICL code (or per drug name when the row has no HICL). The most frequent observed name is cleaned of strengths and dose forms and looked up in RxNorm (exact normalised match, else approximate search), then mapped to ingredients and ATC classes. RxNorm's `HIC_SEQN` is NOT used: it is a different code system (eICU's furosemide code resolves to enoxacin there).

Non-cancelled medication rows: 72,968; keys: 1,500 (1,016 HICL, 484 name-only).

| Match | Keys | Rows | Share of rows |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| exact | 738 | 53,696 | 73.6% |
| approximate | 272 | 14,106 | 19.3% |
| unmapped | 490 | 5,166 | 7.1% |

268 HICL keys (3,929 rows) are named only through `admissiondrug` (home medications); check those names apply.

**The `atc` columns are hints only.** RxClass returns every ATC class whose products contain an ingredient, combinations included (diphenhydramine comes back under M01A NSAIDs via ibuprofen combinations). Do not read them as a drug's own class.
